post.description: Renders the operations to SQL (names quoted, expressions as given, each exactly one SQL expression) and runs them on one of the branch's Postgres databases as the owner (Admin only) or, with `role`, as that role (the SQL editor's session: your member role, then `SET ROLE`), in one transaction with `lock_timeout` (`lock_timeout_ms`, default 5000) and `statement_timeout` (60 s; 15 s for a dry run). A dry run runs the same statements and always rolls back; it evaluates your expressions (defaults, checks, `USING`), so their non-transactional side effects (e.g. `nextval`) remain. A statement that may rewrite a table over `CHELABASE_TABLE_API_DRY_RUN_MAX_BYTES` (default 256 MiB), and every one after it, is only rendered in a dry run (`skipped`), and then `would_succeed` is null. A table the request names that doesn't exist (and no earlier operation creates) is 404 with its `op_index`. Drops end `RESTRICT` and a request with drops returns `dependents`: what `CASCADE` would also remove beyond the request's own drop targets and their parts, and their `hash`. When something depends on a drop and the request confirms no cascade, the dry run and the real run alike answer 409 `has_dependents` with `dependents`, and change nothing. To cascade, send that hash as `cascade.dependents_hash`: the run (dry or real) locks the drop targets' tables, reads the dependents again, and refuses with 409 `dependents_changed` when they differ or when Postgres reports dropping anything but them and the parts of the request's other drop targets (drops that reach each other, e.g. a parent table and its child, need the hash of no dependents); a drop whose target an earlier drop of the request already removed is `skipped` (`already_dropped`). A `CONCURRENTLY` index operation must be the request's only operation: it runs outside a transaction (`statement_timeout` 900 s; a dry run only checks it), can't cascade, and when its build fails after creating its index, that INVALID index is dropped (another index of the same name never is). Postgres errors keep their fields (`op_index`, `sqlstate`, `message`, `detail`, `hint`, `position`; `dry_run: true` on a dry run). Each request is logged with its operation count, never its SQL.

200.description: The statements (executed or skipped, with their notices, rewrite flag and lock), the dependents of the request's drops, whether the dry run would succeed (`null` when something was skipped) and whether the change was committed

Postgres's failures carry `op_index`, `sqlstate`, `message`, `detail`, `hint`, `position`

When the run ends (however it ends), its session is ended, whatever the script made as the member role itself is handed to `role`, and every privilege, default privilege or policy naming the member role is dropped. An Admin acting as a role a member role can't hold (LOGIN, owner-level, or reaching a reserved role) uses the owner's connection and `SET ROLE`; naming the owner runs as the owner. The script is sent unchanged as one simple query, so multi-statement scripts, explicit transactions and commands like `VACUUM` work. Unless `confirm` is true, risky statements (drops, truncates, `DELETE`/`UPDATE` without `WHERE`, also under `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` or `PREPARE`, and anything that doesn't parse) and, on a protected branch, every statement that isn't a read are held back with 409 `sql_confirm_required`. Errors before the connection opens are JSON; then the answer is `200 application/x-ndjson`, one JSON event per line: `notice`, `columns` (`statement`, `columns: [{name, type}]`), `rows` (`statement`, at most 200 rows of text-or-null values), `complete` (`statement`, `tag`, `rows`, `truncated`: over 1,000 rows), `error` (`statement`, `code`, `message`, `detail`, `hint`, `position`: 1-based in the sent text), `heartbeat` (after 15 s without another event) and, always last, `done` (`outcome`: `ok`, `error`, `cancelled`, `timeout` or `truncated_response` past 10 MiB; `duration_ms`). Closing the stream cancels the run. Every run is logged with its command tags and a SHA-256 of the script, never the script.

Teams of the tenant the member joins (at most 50 after duplicates are dropped); empty is

endpoint.

guard_logins.description:
The "guard login roles" switch: on a protected branch, login roles other than the
owner, member logins and the branch's guard exemptions can't change the schema. Copied
from the parent when the branch is made.

history_start.description: Where the branch's history begins (null when unknown); Studio's lower bound for a point.

main_database_missing.description:
A ready branch with no recorded main database: it was dropped in SQL. The data API is
unavailable on the branch until a database of the main name exists again.

protected.description:
A protected branch can't be deleted or reset to its parent (restore still works), and
its database can't be deleted. Set with `updateBranch`.

review_acknowledged_hash.description:

when none was.

retried), `on` or `error` (see `data_api_error`).

data_api_error.description: Why the last enable failed; null otherwise.

default_schema.description: The schema a request to this database uses when it names none.

main.description: The branch's main database: always served by the data API.

owner.description: The Postgres role that owns it.

BranchId.description: Stable identifier for a branch of a database; main's equals its database id.

BranchRole.description: A role of a branch, without secrets. The owner comes first.

blocked_keys.description:
Live data API secret keys that name this role while it is owner-level: the keys the
data API refuses (empty for a plain role).

bypass_rls.description: BYPASSRLS on its own (an owner-level role has it too, through the owner's attributes).

connection_limit.description: The most connections the role may hold at once; `-1` is no limit.

guard_exempt.description:
Listed in the branch's guard exemptions (by name): on a protected branch with "guard
login roles" on, this login role may still change the schema.

inherit.description: INHERIT: the role uses its groups' privileges without `SET ROLE`.

level.description:
`owner_level`: superuser, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB, REPLICATION, or a member of
`neon_superuser` at any depth. Such a role can't back a data API secret key. BYPASSRLS
alone isn't owner-level (see `bypass_rls`).

login.description: Whether the role has the LOGIN attribute.

member_admin.description:
Those of `member_of` with the ADMIN option: the role can grant the group on (I2). A role
holding it is Admin-only to grant (R30).

member_no_set.description:
Those of `member_of` without the SET option: the role can't `SET ROLE` to them, though
it still inherits their privileges (I2).

member_of.description: The roles it's a direct member of, by name (`neon_superuser` isn't listed).

origin.description: The branch's owner, a role made in SQL, or one made through the API.

password.description:
Whether the password can be shown (`generated`), was set in SQL, or is an unusable MD5
hash.

pending.description: Written but not yet applied to the compute; applied when the compute next runs.

valid_until.description: When the role's password stops working; `null` is never.

oneOf.description: The item stays out of the plan.
The plan moves the target's version to the source's (data loss is flagged).
Only for column order conflicts: the target's columns first, then the source's.
Replaces the item in the plan.

own_sql.description: Replaces the item in the plan.

ChoiceBody.description: How the user settles one conflict.

collation.description: Qualified collation name, only when it isn't the type's default.

type_oid.description: `atttypid`: lets the analysis follow a renamed user type (an enum) that existed at the base.

enum.description: Qualified enum name (`schema.name`) when the column is an enum.

oneOf.description: When the column references a stored object (left out otherwise).

ConnectionDetails.description: How to connect to a branch as one of its roles.

ca_file.description:
Self-hosted mode only: the file holding the dev proxy's CA certificate, for
`sslrootcert=` (the URI keeps `sslmode=verify-full`). Null in platform mode.

password.description: Null when it can't be shown; `password_state` says why.

password_state.description:
`generated`: made by Chelabase, shown here. `set_in_sql`: set in SQL, only its hash is
stored; reset it to get a shown one. `md5_unusable`: an MD5 hash, which Chelabase's proxy
can't use; set a new password. `unreadable`: the stored password could not be opened
(a rename or branch copy dropped it); reset it.

uri.description:
Without a password when `password` is null. The user and database are
percent-encoded.

database.description:
The Postgres database; null is the branch's main database. The tree may name it
instead (both must then agree).

role.description: The role to run as; null runs as the database's owner.

tree.description: A data API request: the same JSON `POST /data/v1/query` takes.

columns.description: `conkey`, in order (empty for a table-level check without columns).

oneOf.description: A foreign key's referenced table and columns.

email_verified.description: Default true: the address counts as verified and no email is sent.

oneOf.description: A point in the parent's history; its present when omitted.
The branch to start from; main when omitted.

project_id.description: The project to create it in; the caller needs Admin on it.

CreateFunctionDeploymentRequest.description: A deployment: the bundle manifest (the runtime's format) and its hash.

activate.description:
Make it the active deployment on the branch (default true). The function stays enabled
or disabled as it was; a new one starts disabled.

manifest.description: The bundle manifest, as the runtime loads it. Stored byte for byte as sent.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the manifest's bytes as sent, lowercase hex.

delivery.description: How the invitee gets the link. Default `email`.

grants.description: One grant per project at most; none is fine (the person starts with no access).

team_ids.description:
Teams of the tenant the person joins (at most 50 after duplicates are dropped; each
must be a team of the tenant, else 422 naming it in `team_id`); empty is none. The
grants and the teams are checked together on the person's union, per project.

databases.description:
The Postgres databases the key may reach: 1 to 20 databases of the branch, disabled ones
included. Absent or null is every served database.

database.description: The Postgres database to merge; the branch's main one when omitted.

delivery.description: How the invitee gets the link. Default `email`.

team_ids.description:
Refused in any form, `[]` and `null` included (422 `invalid_request`): only a tenant
admin's invite (`createInvite`) attaches teams (MH-8).

name.description: 1 to 64 characters; the slug is made from it.

CreateRoleRequest.description: A role to create. Only the attributes listed here can be set; any other field is refused.

bypass_rls.description: BYPASSRLS: the role ignores row-level security. Default `false`.

login.description:
LOGIN, with a generated password. `false` makes a NOLOGIN role (a group) with no
password. Default `true`.

member_of.description:
Roles to make it a member of. Each must exist and be the owner's to grant; never one of
Chelabase's own (`authenticator`, `anon`, `authenticated`, `neon_superuser`,
`chelabase_…`), the owner, a `pg_…` role, or the role itself.

owner_level.description:
Makes the role owner-level, like the branch owner: CREATEROLE, CREATEDB, BYPASSRLS
and REPLICATION, and a member of `neon_superuser`. Default `false`.

valid_until.description: When the password stops working. Default: never.

name.description: 1-120 characters after trimming; unique per user and database, ignoring case.

pg_database.description: The Postgres database the editor last ran it in (up to 63 bytes; empty is stored as null).

role.description: The role the editor last ran it as (up to 63 bytes; empty is stored as null); absent: the owner.

bucket.description: Only objects of this bucket (by name, 1-100 bytes).

prefix.description: Only object names starting with this (1-1024 bytes).

url.description:
Where events are POSTed: `https` (`http` only where the operator allows it), at most
2048 bytes, no credentials, resolving only to public addresses.

name.description: Trimmed; 1 to 80 characters, unique in the tenant ignoring case.

CreatedDataKey.description: A key just made, with its plaintext.

databases.description: The Postgres databases the key may reach; null is every served database.

DataApiExposure.description:
One grant that exposes its privileges to the data API (P31): the operation, its grantee
and one shortest membership chain from `anon` or `authenticated` to it (`[anon]` when the
grantee is `anon` itself).

DataApiSchema.description: The Data API schema: everything the asking roles can reach.

oneOf.description: The table app users are mirrored into, when the branch has one (left out otherwise).

DataApiState.description: Whether the data API serves a database of a branch.

DataKey.description: A key as listed: `key` only for the public key.

bypasses_rls.description:
A secret key whose role has BYPASSRLS: it reads and writes past row-level security
(allowed; Studio marks the key). As the role was when the key was made or rotated, kept
up to date by the worker's resync. Always false for the public key.

databases.description: The Postgres databases the key may reach; null is every served database.

managed_by_function.description:
The function whose run-as key this is (edge functions m3): it can't be rotated,
revoked or narrowed here. Absent for every other key.

role_blocked.description:
A secret key whose role is owner-level (superuser, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB, REPLICATION or a
`neon_superuser` member): the data API refuses it. Always false for the public key.

branch_count.description: Live `normal` branches, main included (backups and deleted branches don't count).

history_window.description: Seconds of history the database keeps.

postgres_database.description:
The main Postgres database's name: the display name with every character outside
`[A-Za-z0-9_]` turned into `_` ("web-1 prod" is `web_1_prod`). Merges
(`MergeSummary.database`) and SQL name this one. `null` only for a name Postgres can't use.

storage_max_connections.description: Connections the storage service may hold to each branch.

DatabaseId.description: Stable identifier for a provisioned database instance.

DatabaseSettings.description: A database's settings after a change.

history_window.description: Seconds of history the database keeps.

DatabaseSummary.description: Public database fields only: never credentials or container ids.

postgres_database.description:
The main Postgres database's name: the display name with every character outside
`[A-Za-z0-9_]` turned into `_` ("web-1 prod" is `web_1_prod`). Merges
(`MergeSummary.database`) and SQL name this one. `null` only for a name Postgres can't use.

DefaultObject.description: The objects a default privilege applies to.

DefaultPrivileges.description: One `pg_default_acl` row's entries for the read's role.

confirm.description: The project's slug, typed to confirm.

successor.description: The role that received the objects.

Delivery.description: How an invite reaches the invitee.

description.description:
Postgres's own description (`pg_describe_object`), the text its
`drop cascades to …` notices print.

ErrorBody.description:
The documented shape of the `error` object. Some codes add extra keys (for example
`keys`), which are documented per code.

ErrorCode.description: Stable, machine-readable error code. Serialises as snake_case.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The schema error responses reference: `{"error": ErrorBody}`.

ExpectedAcl.description:
The `acl_hash` the privileges read gave `object` (P10): a different hash at apply time is
409 `privileges_changed_since_read`.

FinishRequest.description: The after-merge choice run by hand on a merge applied with drift (E21).

FixAction.description: What a fix does to an item.

Function.description:
A function of the database, with its state on this branch (null fields when it has no
deployment active here).

deployment_id.description: The deployment active on the branch.

last_error.description: The last invocation error on the branch.

run_as_active.description: Whether a live function-managed key backs `run_as_role` on the branch.

run_as_role.description:
The role the function runs as on the branch: its live run-as key's role (which follows
a rename), else the role set; null for none.

FunctionAuth.description:
Who may call the function: `key` (any data key), `app_user` (a signed-in app user, or a
secret key), `public` (anyone, on `/functions/v1/public/{branch_id}/{name}` only).

FunctionDeployment.description: An immutable deployment of a function.

bundle_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the bundle's manifest, lowercase hex.

FunctionKind.description: `function` or `service` (services come with a later milestone).

FunctionRef.description:
A function or procedure: `oid` from the privileges read; `identity` its `regprocedure`
text then (P11). Only the server's own resolution of `oid` reaches SQL.

Grant.description:
One privilege from an ACL (`aclexplode`). Column privileges live on the column
([`Column::grants`]), so a column's identity (table OID + attnum) carries them through renames.

GrantOverride.description: A narrowing of a grant on one Chelabase database. A `null` field doesn't narrow.

GuardExemptions.description: A branch's guard exemptions, by role name.

Identity.description: An identity column's generation and its sequence (`pg_depend` type `i`).

grants.description: Privileges on the identity sequence (its `relacl`, or the default when NULL).

sequence_name.description: The sequence's name (in the table's schema).

open_signup.description: Whether anyone may sign up (they start with no access). Off by default.

open_signup_switchable.description: Whether this instance lets it be switched on (self-hosted only).

expires_at.description: When its code stops working (72 hours after it was sent); resend it for a new one.

email_available.description: Whether an SMTP server is configured, so `email` delivery works.

oneOf.description: Why not; `null` when it is available.

InviteGrant.description:
A grant an invite carries: a platform role on a project and the Postgres roles it may act
as there.

pg_roles.description:
Postgres role names; for `admin`, which holds every role (R17), checked and dropped.
Never `owner` or the database's owner (the admin platform role includes it), nor a
reserved name. Below admin, only NOLOGIN groups whose memberships reach no owner-level,
LOGIN or reserved role.

invite_url.description:
With `delivery: "link"` and outcome `invited`: the full `/accept-invite` link. It is
shown this once, never stored or logged, and the response is `Cache-Control: no-store`.

MeAdmin.description: A tenant admin to ask for a new invite.

name.description: Their display name; empty when they have none.

MeDatabase.description: The caller's access to one database of a project, where an override narrows it.

platform_role.description: The effective platform role: the grant's, or the lower one the override sets.

role_levels.description: The level each named role is held at on this database, after the override.

roles.description: The effective Postgres roles (`owner` only with the admin role).

id.description: The caller's member id (as `listMembers` names them).

databases.description:
The databases of the project the caller's grant is narrowed on, with what they may do
there. A database not listed has the project's `platform_role` and `roles`.

role_levels.description:
The level each named role is held at (`viewer`, `developer`, `admin`; D1). With `roles`
`"all"` only the roles held below the platform role are listed (a data API role a grant
names); every other role is at `platform_role`.

roles.description:
The Postgres roles the caller may act as on the project: `"all"` for an admin (a tenant
admin, or a project admin, R17), else the names (`owner`, the database's owner, comes
with the admin role). A database
the grant is narrowed on may allow less: see `databases`.

MeResponse.description: The caller and what they may do. Studio only hides what this rules out; the API decides.

email.description: The member's email (null when unknown), else the token's.

instance_admin.description:
Whether the caller may use instance routes (self-hosted: an active tenant admin;
platform: a member of the operator tenant).

oneOf.description:
The caller's membership in the tenant; `None` when they aren't a member (platform mode
makes no members) or the org isn't bound.

name.description: The member's name (null when unknown), else the token's.

projects.description:
Each project the caller may use, with their platform role and the Postgres roles they
may act as there. A tenant admin is Admin with every role on every project.

oneOf.description:
The tenant with the projects the caller may use; `None` when the caller's org isn't
bound to a Chelabase tenant yet.

tenant_admins.description:
The tenant's active admins, for an invited member (an invite that expired before it was
accepted; R49), who can't read the member list but must know whom to ask. Empty for
everyone else.

oneOf.description: `None` when the caller's org isn't bound to a Chelabase tenant yet.

MeRoles.description:
Postgres roles: `"all"` (an Admin's: every role of the branch, the owner included, but not
the data API's `anon` and `authenticated` for acting as them, which need a grant naming
them), or the names.

Member.description: A member of the tenant: a person of the members pool.

accepted_at.description: When an invited member first signed in.

access.description: What the member can reach, over the projects the caller can see.

created_at.description: When the member row was made (an invited member's: when they were invited).

display_name.description:
Empty until the member's first sign-in brings their name (an invitee's is their email's
local part).

email.description:
Lowercased. `null` while unknown, or when another member claimed the address since
(the newest claim wins; it comes back with the member's next request).

has_access.description:
Whether the member can reach anything: a tenant admin, or holding at least one project
grant (an override alone doesn't count). A member without it sees "no access yet".

oneOf.description: The open invite of an invited member (resend or revoke it by its id); `null` otherwise.

suspended_at.description: When the member was suspended; `null` unless suspended (or removed after a suspension).

suspended_by.description:
The member who suspended it; `null` unless suspended, and for a member suspended before
this was recorded.

MemberAccess.description:
What a member can reach, as the caller may see it: only projects the caller can see are
named (a Developer never learns of grants elsewhere), and never a Postgres role or override.

projects.description: The member's platform role on each project the caller can see, by project id.

via.description:
Where the role comes from: `own` (the member's own grant; a tenant admin's admin is
listed the same way), `team` (only through teams) or `both`. The role is the best
source's.

MemberStatusView.description:
Where a member is: `invited` (not signed in yet), `pending` (signed up, waiting for an
admin to approve), `active`, `suspended` (grants kept, no access until a tenant admin
reinstates them), or `removed`.

Merge.description:
A merge with everything the worker computed and the user chose. `analysis`, `plan`,
`rehearsal` and `result` are the schema engine's documents, served as stored.

acknowledgements.description:
Ids of the items (or, for a step that has none, of the step) whose data loss or
security change the user accepts.

analysis.description:
Every changed object with its outcome, the conflicts (base, target and source side by
side) and the reported objects; null while the first compute runs.

base_fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of each normalized schema the analysis is based on; null until computed.

plan.description: The ordered steps by phase (`{steps}`); null until computed, and while conflicts are open.

rehearsal.description: Timings, drift and own-SQL outcomes of the last rehearsal; null when there is none.

result.description:
Created roles, drift and the after-merge outcome; null until the merge finishes. An
abandoned merge (E27) has `leftovers`: what phase 1 left on the target that phase 2
didn't finish (`{kind: not_valid_constraint | not_null_check, schema, table, name}`).

MergeDetail.description: A merge and its log, oldest line first.

MergeLogEntry.description: One line of a merge's log.

MergeOptionsBody.description: Both optional; a missing one stays as it is.

oneOf.description:
What happens to the source branch once the merge is done: kept (default), reset to its
parent or deleted.

lock_timeout_ms.description: `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` of the plan's transaction, 100 to 600000 ms.

MergeState.description:
Where a merge is: `computing` (the worker reads the schemas), `draft` (editable),
`rehearsing`, `rehearsed`, `applying` / `online` / `finishing` (changing the target), and
the end states.

MergeSummary.description: A merge without its analysis and plan: what lists and the answers to actions carry.

failed_phase.description: The phase the merge failed in (`online` can be retried); null otherwise.

rebaselined.description: The base was missing and the target's schema was used instead.

version.description: Changes with every draft save and every recompute: send it back with an edit.

NamedRole.description: A role named by OID and name (owners, grantors, memberships).

ObjectPrivileges.description: One object of the page's schema, with the read's role's entries.

identity.description: A function's or procedure's `regprocedure` text; `None` for the other kinds.

Offered.description:
The privilege names the editor offers per object kind (lower snake case, as the ops take
them; `maintain` only on Postgres 17 and later).

OnDelete.description: What deleting an app user does to their row in the users table.

oneOf.description: `EXECUTE`.

OperationAccepted.description: The 202 body of the routes that start background work: the status the row moved to.

PasswordState.description: Where a role's password stands, as Studio shows it.

PersonalLoginSecret.description: A login with its password, answered once (create and reset).

connection_string.description:
For the main branch's default database. The same login works on every branch where the
member qualifies, with that branch's host.

password.description: Shown this once: it is never stored (only a SCRAM verifier is), listed or logged.

ready_on_main.description:
Whether the login already works on the main branch. When `false` (the compute isn't
running, or the worker didn't answer in time), it works there within seconds.

PersonalLoginView.description:
A member's personal Postgres login on one Chelabase database. Never its password or
verifier.

role_name.description: The Postgres role name, the same on every branch.

valid_until.description: When the password stops working (90 days after its creation or last reset).

PlatformRole.description: A member's platform role on a project. Ordered: Viewer < Developer < Admin.

oneOf.description: A moment, RFC 3339.
A Postgres LSN, `hex/hex`.

PointInTime.description: Where in a branch's history: exactly one of a time or an LSN.

comment.description: T14 minor 14. Absent in a snapshot stored before it was read: `None`.

PrivilegeName.description: A privilege of `alter_default_privileges` (which ones apply depends on the object).

PrivilegeTarget.description: An object whose ACL the privileges read hashes (P10, S3).

PrivilegesPage.description: The privileges read's JSON body (one page).

ProjectGrant.description: A member's grant on a project, with its narrowing overrides on the project's databases.

pg_roles.description:
`"all"` for `admin`: every role on the project (narrowed per database by `overrides`),
except the data API's `anon` and `authenticated` for acting as them, which need a grant
naming them. Below `admin` the names, sorted; a granted role includes every role it can
`SET ROLE` to.

ProjectId.description: Stable identifier for a project within a tenant.

oneOf.description: `null` while app users were never enabled for the project.

slug.description: Chosen from the name when the project is created; renaming doesn't change it.

ProjectStatusView.description: Where a project is in its life.

ProjectTeamGrantView.description: One team's grant on a project, with the team's members (`listProjectTeamGrants`).

pg_roles.description: Sorted; none for `admin`, which holds every role.

database_id.description: The Chelabase database (of this project) that holds the users table.

on_delete.description: What deleting a user does to its row: `delete` (default) or `mark`.

pg_database.description: Defaults to the database's main Postgres database. Fixed once app users are enabled.

schema.description: `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`, default `public`; not a reserved schema. Fixed once enabled.

oneOf.description: Sets how the function is called on this branch (it must have a deployment here).

Defaults to `function` for a new one. Changing an existing function's kind needs Admin,
and only a function without deployments may change it.

PutFunctionSecretRequest.description: A secret's value; it never comes back.

oneOf.description: At most the grant's role.

pg_roles.description:
Postgres role names; for `admin`, which holds every role (R17), checked and dropped.
Never `owner` or the database's owner (the admin platform role includes it), nor a
reserved name. Below admin, only NOLOGIN groups whose memberships reach no owner-level,
LOGIN or reserved role.

name.description:
The login's Postgres role name: `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`, not reserved, and not taken
by any role on any branch of the database nor by another login of it.

ReassignedObjects.description: What a role delete handed to its successor, over every database.

count.description: The objects the role owned (tables, functions, types, schemas, …).

definers.description:
The `SECURITY DEFINER` routines among them, as `schema.name(argument types)`: review
them, they now run as the successor. PUBLIC's EXECUTE on every routine that moved was
revoked.

rebaseline.description: Use the target's current schema as the base (a two-way diff), when the base is gone.

version.description: The `version` you last saw; another one is a 409 `merge_version_conflict`.

Relation.description:
One relation the table API's `getTable` serves: the `Table` shape with the object list's
`ObjectKind` beside its fields. Only an ordinary table
carries constraints, indexes, policies, grants and options; every other kind (a view, a
materialized view, a foreign table, a partitioned table) is read-only and serves its columns
with those lists empty.

ResendInviteRequest.description: The body of `resendInvite`; the whole body may be left out (then `email`).

delivery.description: How the invitee gets the new link. Default `email`.

expires_at.description: When its new code stops working.

invite_url.description:
With `delivery: "link"`: the new `/accept-invite` link. It is shown this once, never
stored or logged, and the response is `Cache-Control: no-store`.

conflict.description: The conflict's id, from the analysis.

RestoreAccepted.description:
The 202 body of a restore: the branch is `resetting`, and its previous state is kept as a
backup branch.

backup_branch_id.description: The backup branch holding the state before the restore.

at.description: The point in the branch's history to rewind to.

Review.description: A branch's review: the items, their hash and the hash last acknowledged.

ReviewFixResponse.description: The SQL a fix ran and the review after it.

digest.description:
The md5 hex of the item's definition (`pg_get_functiondef`, `pg_get_triggerdef` or
`pg_get_ruledef`; `prosrc` for an aggregate), so a body replaced in place changes the
review's hash.

function.description: The function a fix targets, `%I.%I(<identity args>)`: the function itself, or a trigger's function; None for a rule.

identity.description: A function's identity arguments; a trigger's or rule's relation.

new.description: Not in the list last acknowledged (set by the orchestrator).

opaque_body.description: A function whose body can't be followed (not SQL-standard).

ReviewReason.description: One reason, with the referencing object's name (`None` for `security_definer`).

ReviewReasonKind.description: Why an item can run in someone else's session.

revoked.description: The member's personal logins revoked (those that weren't already).

rotated_branches.description: The branches whose member role of this member gets a new password (its sessions end).

RoleDeletePreview.description:
What deleting a role to `successor` would expose: routines and views that would run with
the successor's rights for other roles.

confirm.description:
The token to pass as the delete's `confirm`; `null` when there is nothing to confirm
(no exposures, or `chelabase_orphaned`, which never needs one). It changes whenever the
exposures do.

exposures.description: Sorted by database, kind, identity. Empty when nothing is exposed.

RoleExposure.description:
An object the deleted role owns that would run with the successor's rights for others: a
`SECURITY DEFINER` routine granted to roles other than the successor (PUBLIC's EXECUTE is
revoked on every routine that moves), or a view without `security_invoker` (or a
materialized view) granted to anyone but the successor, PUBLIC included.

grantees.description: The roles granted a privilege on it (`PUBLIC` for everyone), sorted.

identity.description:
`schema.name(argument types)` for a routine, `schema.name` for a view, quoted as SQL
quotes it.

RoleExposureKind.description: The kind of an exposed object.

RoleInUseKey.description: A data API key that names an owner-level role; also the `keys` extra of `role_in_use`.

RoleLevel.description:
What a role may do: `OwnerLevel` is superuser, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB, REPLICATION, or
`neon_superuser` at any depth (E33; BYPASSRLS alone is an attribute, not owner level: a
secret key may use such a role).

RoleOrigin.description:
Where a `neon_roles` row came from: the branch's owner, a role made in SQL, one made
through the API, or a personal login (made by the worker and marked, RT4-4).

RoleRef.description: A grantee or policy role: `PUBLIC` (grantee 0, `polroles = {0}`) or a role.

RoleSessionView.description: One session open as the role (a `pg_stat_activity` row).

application_name.description: The client's `application_name` (empty when it set none).

client_addr.description: The client's address; `null` for a connection from inside the compute.

RoleSessions.description: The live sessions of a role on the branch's compute (E29a).

compute_running.description:
Whether the branch's compute is running. When it isn't, nothing was read (the read
never starts it): `count` is 0 and `sessions` is empty.

count.description: How many sessions are open as the role right now.

confirm.description: `true` runs statements the guard would hold back.

database.description: The Postgres database; null or absent is the branch's main database.

role.description: The role to `SET ROLE` to first; null or absent runs as the owner.

run_id.description: Chosen by the client; names the run for `…/sql/runs/{run_id}/cancel`.

sql.description: The script, sent as one simple query: 1 byte to 1 MiB.

data_api_exposure.description:
P31: the request's grants (default privileges included) to `anon` or `authenticated`,
or to a role either of them inherits, in operation order; empty when none.

SchemaEntry.description: One schema's tables, functions (overloads by name) and enums (labels by name).

SchemaPrivilege.description: A schema privilege of the privilege ops.

SchemaPrivileges.description: One schema's own ACL entries for the read's role.

SequencePrivilege.description: A sequence privilege of the privilege ops.

oneOf.description: A `storage.object_ref`: the object's bucket id and name.
An object's id: a single-column foreign key to `storage.objects(id)`.

An object's name in one bucket: a text column whose comment says
`@storage_ref bucket=<bucket>`.

StorageRefDesc.description: How a column references a stored object (object storage).

StorageWebhook.description: An endpoint, as the API shows it (never its secret).

bucket.description: Only objects of this bucket (by name); `null`: every bucket.

disabled_reason.description:
Why it is disabled: `member` (through the API) or `failing` (three days of failed
attempts); `null` while enabled.

enabled_since.description: When delivery last (re)started: events from then on are delivered.

failing_since.description: The start of the current run of failed attempts; `null` after a success.

prefix.description: Only object names starting with this; `null`: every name.

attempt.description: 1 for the first delivery of the event, then one more per retry.

status.description: The HTTP status, when there was an answer.
The endpoint's HTTP status, when it answered.

StorageWebhookWithSecret.description: An endpoint with its signing secret: shown only here, once.

secret.description:
The signing secret (`whsec_…`): verify each delivery's `Chelabase-Signature` with it.
It can't be read again; rotate it to get a new one.

constraints.description: Every `pg_constraint` row of the table (PG17 has no NOT NULL constraints there).

grants.description: Table-level privileges (`relacl`, or `acldefault('r', relowner)` when NULL).

indexes.description: Indexes that don't back a constraint (`conindid`).

TableDesc.description: A table, view or foreign table. `privileges` (role to held privileges) is `null` unless asked for.

primary_key.description:
The primary key's columns, in the key's order; left out when there is none (a view,
or a table without a key).

TableIndex.description:
An index, in normalized parts so its name isn't part of its definition (a rename is only a
name change).

keys.description:
Key columns or expressions, in order, each as in `CREATE INDEX` (with collation,
operator class and ordering when not the default).

TablePrivilege.description:
A table or column privilege. Its OpenAPI name is `TablePrivilege`: the data API's schema
has a `Privilege` of its own.

description.description: At most 500 characters; empty when it has none.

member_ids.description:
The members' ids, by id. In `getTeam`, the writes' answers and `listMemberTeams`; absent
from `listTeams`.

name.description: Trimmed, 1 to 80 characters, unique in the tenant ignoring case.

projects.description: The team's grants on the projects the caller can see, by project id.

pg_roles.description:
Postgres role names; for `admin`, which holds every role (R17), checked and dropped.
Never `owner` or the database's owner, a reserved name or a personal login. Below admin,
only NOLOGIN groups whose memberships reach no owner-level, LOGIN or reserved role, for
every member of the team on every database (with their own grant and overrides).

TeamProjectAccess.description: What a team gives its members on one project.

pg_roles.description:
The Postgres roles, sorted (none for `admin`, which holds every role); `null` unless
the caller is a tenant admin or an Admin of the project.

display_name.description: The tenant's chosen name; `null` means show the slug.
`null` when it has none: show the slug.

email.description: A new address, verified unless `email_verified` is false.

email_verified.description:
With `email`, whether the new address is verified (default true); alone, sets the flag
on the current address.

UpdateBranchRequest.description: At least one of `protected` and `guard_logins`; `review_hash` only with `protected: true`.

guard_logins.description: The "guard login roles" switch (see the branch's `guard_logins`).

protected.description:
`true` refuses deleting the branch, resetting it to its parent and deleting its
database; restore still works. Protecting runs the branch's review (it needs a running
compute) and needs `review_hash` when the review lists anything.

review_hash.description: The `hash` of the review (`getBranchReview`) the caller saw; stored as acknowledged.

UpdateDatabaseRequest.description: All optional; a missing one is left as it is. `history_window` is in seconds.

storage_max_connections.description: Connections the storage service may hold to each branch, apart from `max_connections`.

active_deployment_id.description:
Makes one of the function's deployments the active one (a rollback, or a deploy made
with `activate: false`).

enabled.description: Turns the function on or off on the branch.

run_as_role.description:
The role the function runs as: a function-managed secret key for it is made (and the
previous one revoked); null clears both. A role with BYPASSRLS needs Admin.

UpdateKeyRequest.description:
Which databases a key may reach. `databases` has no default, so an empty body can't widen a
key to every database by accident.

databases.description:
The Postgres databases the key may reach (1 to 20 databases of the branch, disabled ones
included), or null for every served database. Required.

tenant_admin.description:
Only an active member may become a tenant admin; the last active tenant admin can't
step down.

UpdateMergeRequest.description: Every field but `version` is optional; a missing one stays as it is.

version.description: The `version` you last saw; another one is a 409 `merge_version_conflict`.

default_schema.description: The schema a request to this database uses when it names none: `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$`.

grant_existing.description:
Also grant the data API roles on the objects already in the schema (default false).
Without it, only objects created from now on get grants (through default privileges),
plus, once per database, the first schema's existing objects (a database whose first
enable ran while its schema was missing gets that full first grant once the schema
exists, flag or not). Grants only: it never revokes anything. Sent with an unchanged
`default_schema` it grants on that schema's existing objects now, and answers 409
`data_api_disabled` when the database isn't served.

UpdateRoleRequest.description: A change to a role: only the fields given change.

login.description:
Turning LOGIN on generates a password (read it with the connection details and
`role`); turning it off drops the password.

member_of.description:
The new list of the role's other memberships, with the create's rules
(`pg_*` and Chelabase's own groups stay).

owner_level.description: Owner-level on (CREATEROLE, CREATEDB, BYPASSRLS, REPLICATION, `neon_superuser`) or off.

pg_database.description: `null` or `""` clears the hint; absent leaves it.

role.description: `null` or `""` clears the hint; absent leaves it.

version.description: The version the client last saw; a mismatch answers 409 `saved_query_conflict`.

bucket.description: `null` clears the filter; absent leaves it.

enabled.description:
`false` stops delivery; `true` restarts it from now (events in between are not sent) and
clears the failure state.

prefix.description: `null` clears the filter; absent leaves it.

description.description: At most 500 characters. Left out: unchanged.

name.description: Trimmed; 1 to 80 characters, unique in the tenant ignoring case. Left out: unchanged.

display_name.description:
Trimmed; at most 80 characters, no control characters. An empty or `null` value clears
it. The field itself is required.

UserStepBody.description: SQL the user inserts into the plan.

after.description: The step it follows (generated or user); null puts it at the start of its phase.

id.description:
The user's own id for the step: without `:`, `.` or control characters, and not
`phase1` (the plan's own ids and the merge's log use them).
